newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan to export medicines to Iraq via Jordan.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to export medicines to Iraq via Jordan.

text.p: The state-run Trading Corp of Pakistan (TCP) said on Saturday it had invited bids to be submitted by June 11 for the export of Pakistan-origin medicines to Iraq via Jordan on credit.

A TCP official said shipment would be by air for delivery on a CIF (cost, insurance and freight) basis at Amman international airport in Jordan. He did not indicate the quantity or delivery date of the planned exports.

They would be Pakistan's first official exports of medicine to Iraq since the 1991 Gulf war, although a pharmaceuticals dealer said some Pakistanis had sent medicine to Iraq three years ago with the approval of the U.N. sanctions committee.
Iraq said on Friday it had completed the export of limited amounts of oil under its six-month deal with the United Nations to allow imports of food, medicine and other humanitarian goods.
The United Nations imposed stringent sanctions on Iraq for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
